slides.heading: Year 1 — Autumn 2, Week 3
slides.sub: New content taught directly, practised in words/sentences and applied in reading and dictation.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "e-e" (/iː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="centipede" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="centipede"><path d="M-30 10q10-20 20 0t20 0" fill="none" stroke="#88283f" stroke-width="11" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Evie Egg waits quietly at the end of the word, and when it's time she rolls her sound back over the consonant to wake up the 'e' at the front so it says its own name, 'ee'.

character.name: Evie Egg
character.blurb: Evie Egg sits at the end of the word like a small egg tucked at the end of a nest, sending her sound back across the gap to her matching 'e'.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ee' in tree and 'ea' in tea — here the letters split apart around a consonant, so it's called a split digraph.
slides.formation_cue: This sound splits in two: write 'e', then a consonant, then 'e' again at the end — like these, where the two 'e's sit at opposite ends holding the middle letters between them.
slides.action: Children hold their hands far apart, then bring them together slowly while saying a long 'ee', as if the two ends are calling to each other.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="centipede" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="centipede"><path d="M-30 10q10-20 20 0t20 0" fill="none" stroke="#88283f" stroke-width="11" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>

slides.tip: Starts with 'wh' saying /w/, then the 'ere' ending says /air/ — same spelling as 'here', a different sound.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "i-e" (/aɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="kite" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="kite"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Skye Star twinkles at the end of the word and calls her sound back across the gap so the 'i' at the front can say its own name, like looking up and saying 'I see a star!'

character.name: Skye Star
character.blurb: Skye Star is speckled with little spots of light, and she twinkles at the end of the word, calling back to wake the 'i' at the front.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'igh' in night and 'ie' in tie — here the letters split apart around a consonant, so it's called a split digraph.
slides.formation_cue: This sound splits in two: write 'i' with its dot, then a consonant, then 'e' at the end — like time, where 'i' and 'e' sit either side of the middle letters like two stars at opposite ends of the sky.
slides.action: Children look up and point to the sky, then trace a line from their pointing finger back down to their chest while saying 'i' like naming themselves.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="kite" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="kite"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: A plum is sweet and ripe.

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.dictation: The moon looks like a boat.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.dictation: Some of the plums are ripe.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.

slides.dictation: Her shirt is blue and white.
